name: Purchasing power parity
definition: A way to compare buying power across places by accounting for differences in prices. PPP-based international dollars are comparison units, not US dollars you can exchange at a bank. A 2011 reference means the series uses that purchasing-power benchmark; it does not mean the observation occurred in 2011.

name: Consumer Price Index
definition: An index tracking changes in the prices of a representative consumer basket over time. The Atlas uses US CPI for its constant-dollar display. This is different from measuring local purchasing power or how many local basic-needs baskets a wage buys.

name: Gross domestic product
definition: Economic output produced within a territory during a period, usually one year here. GDP per person divides annual output by population. It is not a wage, household income or accumulated wealth.

name: Human Development Index
definition: An index combining health, education and income dimensions. It does not measure happiness or capture every aspect of wellbeing. Historical reconstructions and other development indices retain their own definitions in the evidence.

name: Foreign exchange
definition: Conversion between currencies. The Atlas uses the money record's own year and the stated exchange-rate source. Exchange conversion alone does not adjust for inflation; displayed rates are rounded while calculations keep the original precision.

name: United States dollar
definition: The currency of the United States. Nominal USD is money valued at the stated year's prices. Constant USD adjusts for price changes to a stated base year. Neither is the same as a PPP international dollar.

name: Pound sterling
definition: The currency of the United Kingdom. An exchange quote such as 1 GBP = 4.40 USD means one pound converts to about 4.40 US dollars using the stated rate and year.

name: Euro
definition: The currency used by euro-area members. Historical series expressed retrospectively in euros require their own conversion method; a modern euro rate cannot simply be applied to earlier currencies.

name: World Development Indicators
definition: The World Bank's collection of development indicators. Each series has its own source, definition, geography and coverage; the WDI label alone does not guarantee comparable records for every country and year.

name: Bank for International Settlements
definition: The institution providing the historical sterling exchange-rate series used by the Atlas. Follow the record's evidence link for the original quote, annual averaging method and underlying national sources.
